why: A, C and D are true statements that any common slip (dropping the £2.7m contractor cost, using cumulative shares, treating user counts as cumulative) makes look false, and none of those slips leaves B as the only false statement.
B over-reads the higher margin as a higher profit, D over-reads the higher staff-cost percentage as a larger amount, and C (rents) is the one statement without basis that sourceHas lists.

Ranking by profit alone lands on the correct option, but sourceHas names that same slip; C and D each come from misreading one row of an equal-store pair (A/D, B/C), and A is the single ranking filler sourceHas allows.

5 clubs comes from assuming Large-Market clubs offset Small-Market ones one for one, 4 from balancing the $17.6m total profit while leaving out the Mid-Market clubs, and 2 continues the spacing of that grid.
$245 leaves out classes 1 and 2, and the options form a tight grid (steps of $28, about 9% of $301), so rough estimates and slips land on the neighbours.

Reading only Region 2 (the single-region slip that option C invites with Region 6's 10%) gives 95% for the three products, so A is true and no other statement is, and sourceHas names only the simple-average slip.

B takes the urgent-care share as a share of all animals (wrong base), C's 6.0% comes from rounding 32% to a third (18% ÷ 3), and D (onward referral to surgery) is the one statement without basis that sourceHas lists.

A takes the technical-support share as a share of all callers (wrong base), D is a near miss that rounds 9.87% up to 10%, and C (transfers to sales) is the one statement without basis that sourceHas lists.
B and D use the 5.8bn litres that reach customers as the base (giving 10.3% and 13.8%), and C's 18% comes from counting bars 3 to 5 as business use and leaving out factories (1.3 ÷ 7.3).

1.2 is the antivirus share loss averaged over three years (wrong series), 3.8 is the antivirus total loss without averaging, and 1.6 is the cloud backup total loss (about 1.5) without dividing by the years; no common slip lands within 20% of 0.5.
